notes: Evidence is limited to numbered Sanskrit verses and their translations on the cited Vedabase chapter pages. Chapter synopses and purports are not claim sources.

In 8.10, individually named demons in 8.10.19–24 are represented as named captains around Bali. Plural collectives such as the sons of Puloma, Kāleyas, and other demon/god classes are omitted; the unnamed hundred sons of Bali are not split into individuals.

For Canto 8.1 and 8.13, plural classes such as Yāmas, Satyas, Satyavratas, Vaidhṛtis, Sutapās, Maruts, and other unnamed sages/demigods are not modeled as people. A named individual listed in a roster is retained only when the verse gives a personal name.

Homonyms are branch-scoped: the Canto 8 battle names remain local where identity with a similarly named figure elsewhere is not established by these verses. Clear anchors (Brahmā, Kaśyapa, Vivasvat, Indra, Vasiṣṭha, Garuḍa, Bali, Virocana) are reused where passage context is explicit. Maya Dānava is the rostered Maya of 8.10.19–24; Durgādevī is one figure also called Bhadra Kālī. The Aśvinī twins are not individuated because this passage does not name them.
Manvantara predictions in 8.13 remain future claims in the source narrative; claims report the text’s stated future roles/relationships and do not imply historicity.
